posts.topic: Forty pages, no enquiries
posts.why: The number contrast is the whole argument.

tiktok.hook: This site has forty pages and has never had one enquiry.
beats: Because pages are not a funnel
tiktok.vo: This site cost twenty five thousand naira, has forty pages, and in eight months has had no enquiries. Forty pages is not forty chances. It is forty places for the customer to get lost. One page that answers six questions and asks for one action would outperform the entire thing, and it would take an afternoon.
tiktok.cap: Forty pages, zero enquiries. Pages are not a funnel.

instagram.cap: Volume of pages is not the same as a path to buying.

facebook.body:
A site I looked at this week: ₦25,000, forty pages, zero enquiries in eight months.

Forty pages is not forty chances. It is forty places for a customer to get lost.

One page that answers six questions and asks for one clear action would beat the whole thing, and it takes an afternoon to write.

How many pages does your site have, and how many enquiries?

posts.topic: The cheapest quote is a payment plan
posts.why: A reframe that sticks because it is financially literal.

tiktok.hook: The cheapest quote is a payment plan for a second project.
tiktok.vo: The cheapest quote is a payment plan for a second project. You pay the small number now, then you pay a bigger number later to fix what the small number could not do, and you lose six months in between. Which means the cheap option is not cheap, it is just earlier.
tiktok.cap: You will pay twice. The first payment is just quieter.

instagram.cap: Cheap work is a deposit on the work you actually needed.

facebook.body:
The cheapest quote is usually a payment plan for a second project.

You pay the small number now. Then you pay a bigger number later to fix what the small number could not do. And you lose six months in between, which is the part nobody puts in the invoice.

So it was never cheaper. It was just earlier.

Have you paid twice for anything?

posts.topic: Ask what happens after launch
posts.why: One question that exposes most cheap quotes instantly.

tiktok.hook: Before you accept any web quote, ask what happens after launch.
tiktok.vo: Before you accept any web quote, ask one question: what happens after launch. Ask who updates the price list, who fixes the contact form when it breaks, and who answers the message in March. Most cheap quotes stop at delivery, which is why they are cheap, and then you discover the cost in the third month when you need one line changed.
tiktok.cap: The quote ends at launch. The business does not.

instagram.cap: Ask this before you pay anyone for a website. Save it.

facebook.body:
Before you accept any website quote, ask one question: what happens after launch?

Who updates the price list? Who fixes the contact form when it breaks? Who answers you in March?

Most cheap quotes stop at delivery. That is why they are cheap, and you find out the real cost in the third month when you need one line changed.

The quote ends at launch. Your business does not.

What would you ask?

posts.topic: I'll do it myself with AI
posts.why: Speaks directly to a real 2026 objection.

tiktok.hook: "I'll do it myself with AI" costs two months and one relaunch.
beats: Two months later you pay someone
tiktok.vo: I will do it myself with AI costs two months and one relaunch. The tool is free. The decisions are not. Which photo goes first, what the price says, which of six headlines is true, what to delete. Two months in you still have not chosen, so you pay someone to choose, and the free tool turns out to be the most expensive part.
tiktok.cap: The tool is free. Deciding what to say is the work.

instagram.cap: AI will write you six options. It will not pick one for your customer.

facebook.body:
'I'll just do it myself with AI' costs about two months and one relaunch.

The tool is free. The decisions are not. Which photo goes first. What the price says. Which of six headlines is actually true. What to delete.

Two months in, you still have not chosen, so you pay someone to choose — and the free tool turns out to be the expensive part.

What is the decision you keep avoiding?

posts.topic: Paid twice for the same website
posts.why: A concrete case with a real number, labelled as our client's story.

tiktok.hook: A business paid twice for the same website.
tiktok.vo: A business paid twice for the same website. The first one was thirty thousand naira and it did not work on a phone, which is where all their customers were. Eighteen months of nobody buying later, they paid properly, and the second site cost three times the first. The first quote was not cheap. It was a deposit.
tiktok.cap: ₦30,000, then ₦90,000 for the same site. The first quote was a deposit.

instagram.cap: The cheapest version of a thing is often the most expensive way to get it.

facebook.body:
A business we worked with paid twice for the same website.

The first one was ₦30,000 and did not work on a phone, which is where all of their customers were. Eighteen months of nobody buying later, they paid properly for the second one.

₦30,000 plus ₦90,000 plus eighteen months equals the most expensive website in this story.

The first quote was not cheap. It was a deposit.

What have you paid twice for?

posts.topic: Three questions for any web quote
posts.why: A takeaway they can use on someone else's pitch today.

tiktok.hook: Three questions to ask any web quote, before you pay.
beats: Who fixes it in six months
tiktok.vo: Three questions to ask any web quote. Who owns the domain, in whose name, in writing. Who fixes it when it breaks in six months, and how much do they charge. And who pays for hosting every year. If any of those answers is vague, walk away now, because all three become emergencies at the worst possible time.
tiktok.cap: Domain, fixes, hosting. Ask all three before you pay anyone.

instagram.cap: If you cannot answer all three, you do not own your website.

facebook.body:
Three questions to ask any website quote:

1. Who owns the domain, in whose name, in writing?
2. Who fixes it when it breaks in six months, and at what cost?
3. Who pays for hosting, and how much is it each year?

If any answer is vague, walk away now. All three become emergencies at the worst possible time.

Can you answer all three about your own site today?

posts.topic: A cheap logo is fine. A cheap domain is not.
posts.why: Separates the thing you can skimp on from the thing you cannot.

tiktok.hook: A cheap logo is fine. A cheap domain is not.
beats: If it is not in your name
tiktok.vo: A cheap logo is fine, because you can change a logo in a week. A cheap domain is not, because it is your address. If it is registered in someone else's name, they can take your whole business off the internet with one email, and you have no recourse. Never let anyone else own your name.
tiktok.cap: Your logo can change. Your address cannot be taken.

instagram.cap: Do not let a vendor hold the keys to your business.

facebook.body:
A cheap logo is fine. You can change a logo in a week.

A cheap domain is not fine. It is your address, and if it is registered in someone else's name, they can take your entire business off the internet with one email and you have no recourse.

Check today: whose name is on your domain?

If it is not yours, fix it this week. It takes about twenty minutes.

posts.topic: Cheapest or the one who asked questions
posts.why: Unanimity is the strongest possible evidence.

tiktok.hook: I asked: cheapest quote, or the one who asked questions?
tiktok.vo: I asked people whether they would take the cheapest quote or the one from the person who asked them the most questions. Everyone chose the questions. Every single person. Because being asked questions feels like being understood, and a cheap quote feels like a template. That is what you are competing with, not the number.
tiktok.cap: Everyone chose the one who asked questions. Every single person.

instagram.cap: Questions signal attention. Price signals nothing.

facebook.body:
I asked people: would you take the cheapest quote, or the one from the person who asked you the most questions?

Everyone chose the questions. Every single person.

Being asked questions feels like being understood. A cheap quote feels like a template, because it usually is one.

That is what you are competing with. Not the number.

What questions do you ask before quoting?

posts.topic: Cheap on purpose
posts.why: Owning the low price honestly is more credible than justifying it.

tiktok.hook: Five thousand naira is cheap on purpose. Here is the limit.
beats: No one will build it for you
That is why it is five
tiktok.vo: Five thousand naira is cheap on purpose, and here is the limit. It is a template, not a service. Nobody will build anything for you, nobody will answer questions about your specific business, and if you get stuck there is no call. That is exactly why it costs five thousand and not fifty. If you want the service, that is a different conversation and a different number.
tiktok.cap: ₦5,000 buys a template. Not a service, not a call. Message PACK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

instagram.cap: The price is honest about the product. Read the limit before buying.

facebook.body:
₦5,000 is cheap on purpose. Here is the honest limit.

It is a template, not a service. Nobody builds anything for you. Nobody answers questions about your specific business. If you get stuck at 11pm, there is no call.

That is exactly why it costs ₦5,000 and not ₦50,000.

If you want the service, that is a different conversation with a different number, and I will tell you honestly which one you need.

Message PACK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.topic: A five-page site for forty thousand
posts.why: Naming what a price can buy is more useful than refusing.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked for five pages for forty thousand naira.
beats: Forty thousand does not buy five pages
tiktok.vo: Someone asked for a five page site for forty thousand naira. We said no, and then we said what forty thousand does buy: one page, done properly, with copy, on a phone, with a working contact button. Five pages at that price is five templates nobody reads. They took the one page, and it is the only site they have ever had enquiries from.
tiktok.cap: We refused five pages and sold one. It was the honest answer.

instagram.cap: A smaller promise you can keep beats a bigger one you cannot.

facebook.body:
Someone asked for a five-page website for ₦40,000.

We said no. And then we said what ₦40,000 actually buys: one page, done properly. Real copy. Works on a phone. A contact button that works.

Five pages at that price is five templates nobody reads.

They took the one page. It is the first site they have ever had enquiries from.

Would you rather have five pages or one that works?

posts.topic: Write down who owns what
posts.why: A five-minute task with permanent consequences.

tiktok.hook: Check whose name is on your domain. Then fix it.
beats: Then you cannot be held hostage
tiktok.vo: Write down who owns your domain and your hosting, in one note on your phone, including the login email. If either is in someone else's name, fix it this week while it is calm, not in six months when you have fallen out. This is the least interesting task in your business and the only one that can end it.
tiktok.cap: One note: domain, hosting, logins, who to call. Do it tonight.

instagram.cap: The least interesting task in your business is the one that can end it.

facebook.body:
Write down who owns your domain and your hosting. One note on your phone:

Domain — registered in whose name?
Hosting — paid by whom?
Login email — which one?
Who do I call if it breaks?

If any of those is in someone else's name, fix it this week while everything is calm, not in six months when you have fallen out with them.

Do you know your answers right now?

posts.topic: A spinning logo
posts.why: Every viewer has waited through this exact site.

tiktok.hook: This site opens with six seconds of spinning logo.
tiktok.vo: This site opens with a video of a spinning logo. Six seconds, no words, no product, loading on mobile data at the customer's expense. In the time it takes that logo to finish spinning, the customer has decided you are slow. The animation is not the brand, it is the delay.
tiktok.cap: Six seconds of spinning logo. Nobody has ever bought because of it.

instagram.cap: The first thing on the page should be the offer, not the animation.

facebook.body:
This site opens with a video of a spinning logo.

Six seconds. No words. No product. Loading on the customer's mobile data at the customer's expense.

By the time that logo finishes spinning, they have already decided you are slow.

Put the offer first and let the logo be small and still.

What does your page do in the first three seconds?

posts.topic: Nobody buys because of a loading animation
posts.why: A line that is impossible to argue with.

tiktok.hook: Nobody has ever bought anything because of a loading animation.
tiktok.vo: Nobody has ever bought anything because of a loading animation. Not once, in the history of commerce. People leave because of them all the time. Speed is invisible when you have it and fatal when you do not, and the fix is usually deletion, not optimisation.
tiktok.cap: Nobody bought because of it. People leave because of it.

instagram.cap: Speed is invisible when you have it and fatal when you don't.

facebook.body:
Nobody has ever bought anything because of a loading animation.

People leave because of them constantly.

Speed is invisible when you have it and fatal when you do not. Which means the fix is often deletion, not optimisation — and deletion is free.

What could you delete from your homepage tonight?

posts.topic: The first line has three jobs
posts.why: One rule with three options, easy to apply today.

tiktok.hook: Your first line has three jobs. It can only do one.
tiktok.vo: Your first line has three jobs and it can only do one. Say what you sell, say who it is for, or say what to do next. Most homepages try all three at once and end up saying nothing. Pick the strongest one for your customer and write it in ten words or fewer, then leave it alone for a week.
tiktok.cap: Say what you sell, who for, or what to do. Not all three.

instagram.cap: Ten words or fewer. Then leave it alone for a week.

facebook.body:
Your first line has three possible jobs and can only do one of them well:

1. Say what you sell.
2. Say who it is for.
3. Say what to do next.

Most homepages attempt all three and say nothing.

Pick the strongest one for your customer, write it in ten words or fewer, and leave it alone for a week.

What is your current first line?

posts.topic: Design is reading order
posts.why: Reframes design from taste to function, which suits a non-designer owner.

tiktok.hook: Design is not decoration. Design is reading order.
tiktok.vo: Design is not decoration. Design is reading order. What do they see first, what do they see second, and where does the eye go when they get bored. If the answer is anywhere but the button, the design is decorative and it is costing you. You do not need taste for this, you need to squint at your own page.
tiktok.cap: Squint at your homepage. Whatever you see first is what you are selling.

instagram.cap: Squint at your own page. What survives the blur is the message.

facebook.body:
Design is not decoration. Design is reading order.

What does the customer see first? Second? Where does their eye go when they get bored?

If the answer is anywhere other than the thing you want them to do, the design is decorative and it is costing you money.

You do not need taste to check this. Squint at your own page. Whatever survives the blur is what you are actually selling.

What do you see first?

posts.topic: Better by deleting
posts.why: Removal is the cheapest improvement available, so the story is actionable.

tiktok.hook: A page got four times better by deleting the top half.
beats: Two hundred words about the founder
tiktok.vo: A page got four times better by deleting the top half of it. Two hundred words about the founder and the vision, replaced with one line about what they sell and to whom. Nothing was added. Nothing was designed. The line that had been hiding at the bottom was suddenly the headline, and it turned out to be the best sentence on the site.
tiktok.cap: Nothing added. Half the page deleted. Four times the enquiries.

slides: Best line was at the bottom
instagram.cap: The best sentence on your site is probably already there, buried.

facebook.body:
A homepage got four times better by deleting the top half of it.

Two hundred words about the founder and the vision, replaced with one line about what they sell and who they sell it to.

Nothing was added. Nothing was redesigned. The sentence that had been buried at the bottom became the headline, and it turned out to be the best writing on the site.

What is buried at the bottom of yours?

posts.topic: Put the proof next to the claim
posts.why: A structural fix, not a copywriting opinion.

tiktok.hook: Put the proof next to the claim, not four screens below it.
beats: Proof: the date on the last job
tiktok.vo: Put the proof next to the claim. If you say fast delivery, put the delivery date of your last job on the same line. If you say quality, put the photo of the actual product beside it. A claim on its own is a slogan. A claim with evidence attached is a fact, and facts are the only things that move money.
tiktok.cap: A claim alone is a slogan. A claim with evidence is a fact.

instagram.cap: Every adjective needs a receipt beside it.

facebook.body:
Put the proof next to the claim.

'Fast delivery' — with the date of your last job on the same line.
'Quality you can trust' — with a photo of the actual product beside it.

A claim on its own is a slogan. A claim with evidence attached is a fact, and facts are the only thing that moves money.

Which of your claims has no receipt?

posts.topic: Your best photo is at the bottom
posts.why: Nearly universal, and instantly checkable.

tiktok.hook: Your best photo is at the bottom, where nobody decides.
tiktok.vo: Your best photo is at the bottom of the page. The top is a stock image of people shaking hands, and the bottom is a real photo of the real thing you actually sell. Swap them. That is a free improvement that takes ninety seconds and does more than a redesign.
tiktok.cap: Swap your stock photo for your real one. Ninety seconds.

instagram.cap: The real thing beats the beautiful thing every time.

facebook.body:
Your best photo is almost certainly at the bottom of the page, where nobody makes a decision.

The top has a stock image of people shaking hands. The bottom has a real photo of the real thing you sell.

Swap them. It takes ninety seconds and it does more than a redesign.

What is at the top of your homepage right now?

posts.topic: The last shop you actually bought from
posts.why: Witnesses describing their own behaviour is the proof.

tiktok.hook: I asked people why they bought from the last shop they used.
beats: I saw the price straight away
tiktok.vo: I asked people why they bought from the last shop they used. Almost nobody mentioned design. One person said I saw the price straight away and I knew it was for me, and that was the whole reason. Which means the price and the first line are doing almost all the work, and everything else is decoration.
tiktok.cap: "I saw the price straight away." That was the entire conversion.

instagram.cap: The price and the first line are doing almost all the work.

facebook.body:
I asked people why they bought from the last shop they used.

Almost nobody mentioned design. One person said: 'I saw the price straight away and I knew it was for me.' That was the whole reason.

Which means the price and the first line do almost all of the work. Everything else is decoration.

Why did you buy from the last shop you used?

posts.topic: The blueprint writes the first ten seconds
posts.why: Frames the product as a decision document, not a design file.

beats: Five thousand naira, no design skills

It will not make your page beautiful. It will make it understandable, which is the part that was costing you money. Five thousand naira, and no design skill needed to use it.

instagram.cap: It will not make your page pretty. It will make it understood.

facebook.body:
The Homepage Blueprint is about the first ten seconds of your site, and it is words, not pixels.

Your first line. Your second line. What your button says.

It will not make your page beautiful. It will make it understandable, which is the part that was actually costing you money.

₦5,000. No design skill needed to use it. Message HOMEPAGE on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.topic: Auto-playing sound
posts.why: A refusal everyone has suffered from as a visitor.

tiktok.hook: A client wanted sound to play automatically. We said no.
beats: It is not a mute button
tiktok.vo: A client wanted music to play the moment the site loaded. We said no. On a phone, in public, with the volume up, that is not a feature, it is an exit. They argued for a day, we built it without sound, and the enquiries went up. The fastest way to lose someone on mobile is to make a noise they did not ask for.
tiktok.cap: On a phone with the volume up, sound is not a feature. It is an exit.

instagram.cap: Never make a noise the visitor did not ask for.

facebook.body:
A client wanted music to play automatically when their site loaded.

We said no. On a phone, in public, with the volume up, that is not a feature. It is an exit.

They argued about it for a day. We built it without sound. Enquiries went up.

The fastest way to lose someone on mobile is to make a noise they did not ask for.

What would make you close a site immediately?

posts.topic: Print your homepage
posts.why: A physical test that bypasses design opinion entirely.

tiktok.hook: Print your homepage. Circle what you read first.
tiktok.vo: Print your homepage and put it on the table. Squint. Circle the first thing you read. If it is your logo, start again, because your logo is your name and your name is not your offer. If it is your offer, good. If it is a stock photo, delete it. This takes four minutes and you already have a printer or a phone screen.
tiktok.cap: Print it, squint, circle the first thing. That is your real homepage.

instagram.cap: Four minutes. No printer? Squint at your phone instead.

facebook.body:
Print your homepage and put it on the table. Squint. Circle the first thing you read.

If it is your logo, start again. Your logo is your name, and your name is not your offer.

If it is your offer, good. If it is a stock photo, delete it.

Four minutes. No printer? Screenshot it and squint at your phone.

What did you circle?
